govdocs-archive_org-SatanicRitualSitesUS: This nameless list of devil-grounds in the USA names spots where dark rites are said to be held. The file fits the plot-lore shelf. No proof backs its sayings. Take its lists as unproved. Read it with both eyes open.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-AbelowMartin_Ru: This FBI document on Lee Harvey Oswald — August 1964 — is a Bureau file on the accused assassin. The declassified memo is a primary source on the JFK case. The Bureau watched Oswald before Dallas. Researchers value such files.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-CIARayManuel_CI: Charles Bartlett’s Cuban CIA Critic Sealing Own Fate covers a Cuban critic of the agency. Critics of the agency risked much. The Cold War was unforgiving. The file belongs to the intelligence archive. The item is a fragment of press history.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-GilManuel_Gil_M: Harold Weisberg’s memo to Jim Garrison on Manuel Gil — March 17, 1966 — is a researcher’s note. Weisberg fed Garrison leads. The memo may hold a clue. The file belongs to the assassination archive. The item is a fragment of the record.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-HurwitzMichael_: Michael Hurwitz’s letter to Harold Weisberg — April 5 — is a researcher’s note. Researchers traded findings by mail. The network was vast. The letter may hold a clue. The file belongs to the assassination archive. The item is a fragment of correspondence.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-JamesDaniel_Jam: This letter on FBI FOIA non-compliance — creator unknown — is a file on the records fight. The Bureau fought disclosure for decades. The fight continues. The file belongs to the legal archive. The item is a fragment of the record.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-MajerusMichael_: This handwritten letter fragment — creator unknown — is a personal note. Handwritten notes capture the moment. The note may hold a clue. Archivists value such fragments. The file belongs to the personal archive. The item is a fragment of correspondence.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-MarshMichael_Ma: These fan letters to Michael Marsh on JFK assassination lectures — various authors — are reader mail. Audiences wrote to their lecturers. The letters are warm. The file belongs to the cultural archive. The item is a fragment of correspondence.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-MowerEdgarAnsel: Chalmers M. Roberts’s Panoramas of Our Times — reviews of Krock and Mowrer memoirs — is a Washington Post piece. The memoirs spanned the century’s crises. The file belongs to the literary archive. The item is a fragment of press history.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-PierceSamuel_Pi: This item — Pierce, Samuel — is a National Security Internet Archive file. The file’s full context is unclear. Its subject seems to be the JFK case. The file may hold a clue. Archivists value such fragments. The item is a fragment of the archive.
sleeping-fires-a-novel: Gertrude Atherton, California's queen of letters, wakes this tale of love burning low under smooth, proper lives. Her heroine weighs heart against custom with the bold frankness that made Atherton's name. Worldly, polished fiction, aglow with Jazz Age fire. A sharp, stylish portrait of women testing the bounds of their world.
rudin-a-novel: Turgenev's first novel introduces Rudin — the brilliant, eloquent, fatally indecisive hero who became the type of Russia's superfluous man. He talks beautifully and acts not at all, breaking hearts along the way. A masterful, melancholy portrait that launched one of literature's great careers.
the-sheik-a-novel: E. M. Hull's desert romance — the book that made Rudolph Valentino a star — tells of Diana Mayo, carried off by the proud Sheik Ahmed. Passion in the Sahara made it the most famous romance of its day. Dated now, but a landmark of popular fiction.
a-terrible-secret-a-novel: May Agnes Fleming, the queen of the story papers, weaves a breathless tale around a terrible secret — love, mystery, and startling revelations in every chapter. Her millions of readers devoured such thrilling romances by the score. Victorian popular fiction at its most sensational and fun.
we-can-t-have-everything-a-novel: Rupert Hughes' Jazz Age novel follows bright pleasure-seekers learning that we can't have everything — love, money, and happiness seldom arrive together. His smart, worldly tale catches the fizz and ache of the 1920s. A sparkling period piece, honest and entertaining.
not-george-washington-an-autobiographica: Wodehouse and Westbrook's comic novel pretends to be autobiography — anything but George Washington's. The joke runs through publishing, love, and farce. Early Wodehouse foolery at its silliest. Publishers, poets, and pretty girls whirl through this early comic romp. The co-authors keep the joke spinning with infectious high spirits.
an-american-politician-a-novel: F. Marion Crawford's American Politician dissects Gilded Age politics — bosses, ballots, and a hero's ideals. His cosmopolitan eye found America fascinating. A sharp novel of democracy. Washington lobbies and Newport drawing rooms share his ironic eye. Crawford knew both worlds, and judged each with wit.
poor-white-a-novel: Sherwood Anderson's Poor White follows Hugh McVey, the farmhand inventor whose machines unmake his Ohio town. His brooding tale of industry's human cost is deeply moving. A great American novel of the machine age. Anderson's Ohio town stands for all industrial America.
annie-kilburn-a-novel: William Dean Howells' Annie Kilburn comes home to her New England village determined to do good among the poor. Her well-meant efforts meet ingratitude, pride, and the hard facts of class. Howells' quiet realism examines conscience with rare honesty. A searching novel of social duty from America's dean of letters.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-achitopel: A 1913 entry on Achitopel — Ahithophel, David's counselor turned traitor. Wendell Reilly tells his bitter end. His counsel failed, and he hanged himself. Treason's wages, in one dark life. His counsel was prized as God's own oracle. Absalom's folly ruined them both.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alexandre-vin: This 1913 reference piece on Alexandre Jandel — the restorer of the Dominican Order — honors his rule. Reginald Walsh tells his story. He brought back the old strict life. Houses rose again in France and Italy. Lacordaire stood beside him in the work. The Friars Preachers owe him their rebirth.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alfred-rethel: A 1913 entry on Alfred Rethel — the German painter of history's tragedies. Gerhard Gietmann praises his stark power. His Dance of Death haunts the memory. Aachen's frescoes show his genius. Art's prophet of doom. His frescoes warn from Aachen's walls. His woodcuts spread his fame.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-amraphel: A 1913 entry on Amraphel — the king of Shinar in Genesis. Gabriel Oussani weighs his identity. He warred with the eastern kings. Abraham routed his allied host. A shadowy king of the old East. His name means speaker of judgment. His allies fled before Abraham's men.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-anthony-danie: This 1913 reference piece on Anthony Daniel — the Jesuit martyr of Canada. Edward Spillane honors his death. The Iroquois struck at his mission. He baptized as the flames rose. A martyr of the North American missions. His feast joins the martyrs' roll.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-antoine-cesar: A 1913 entry on Antoine-César Becquerel — the French physicist. William Fox honors his electrical researches. His son and grandson followed his science. The Becquerels were a dynasty of physics. A pioneer of the current's laws. His chair passed to his son.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-antoine-henri: A 1913 entry on Bérault-Bercastel — the historian of the Church. Patricius Schlager notes his twenty-four volumes. His pages carried the story to his day. The entry preserves his modest fame. A chronicler of the Church's tale. His volumes reach the eighteenth century.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-apse-chapel: A 1913 entry on the apse chapel — the radiating chapels of the chevet. Thomas Poole describes their Gothic grace. The pilgrims prayed at each altar. The east end blooms with stone. The crown of the great churches. Their altars honor the local saints.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-augustin-barr: A 1913 entry on Augustin Barruel — the Jesuit memorialist of the Revolution. William Fanning tells his famous Mémoires. He traced the conspiracy's threads. The exiled fathers read his pages. The chronicler of the secret societies. His Jacobinism traced the lodges' plot.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-augustin-jean: This 1913 reference piece on Augustin Fresnel — the founder of wave optics. Henry Brock honors his luminous theory. His lenses guard the lighthouses. The Academy crowned his labors. A Catholic among the physicists. His lighthouse lens saves the sailors. His wave theory conquered the scientists.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-babel: A 1913 entry on Babel — the tower of the confusion of tongues. Anthony Maas unfolds the Genesis tale. The builders' pride scattered the nations. The scholars sift its ancient roots. The Bible's first skyscraper. Its ziggurat inspired the tale. Its moral warns the proud builders.
